div.head: Hn 33.2a
div.ab:
Si uero sine calumpnia recipiatur, et deinceps causam
illam reformare quis cupiat, non procedet in cele[bration]ibus[?], ut opus sit iudicibus narraciones repetere iudicii, maxime si dominus querimonie interfuerit uel dapifer uel minister eius, uel congruum inde terminum habuerit.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 564 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

Corrected November 2026: the words from “illam reformare” to the end of the sentence, printed by Liebermann at the top of p. 565, with his footnotes a and 1–5 on that page, had been put by mistake at the end of Hn 33.2 when the page was transcribed. They continue the sentence of 33.2a (“Si uero sine calumpnia recipiatur, et deinceps causam illam reformare quis cupiat, non procedet …”), as Liebermann’s own note in vol. III, p. 321 (“33, 2a procedit”) confirms, and are given there now.

div.ab: But if it is received without challenge, and afterwards someone wishes to reform that case, he shall not proceed in the cele[bration]s [?], so that the judges need to repeat the narration of the judgment, especially if the lord of the complaint was present, or his steward or officer, or [if] he has had a fitting term for it.
